text.p: Typhoon Carlo, with 100 mph winds, is centered about 175 miles north of Agrihan in the northern Mariana Islands, moving north northwest at 5 mph. As Carlo moves away from the islands, it will only be a threat to shipping. Top winds should peak near 110-115 mph during the next 24 hours before the storm begins to weaken.

Hurricane Lili remains a threat to shipping. The center of the storm is still about 640 miles east of Bermuda but is now moving east southeast at 5 mph. Top winds have increased to 85 mph but should begin to weaken steadily during the next 24-36 hours as the storms moves eastward and loses tropical characteristics.

Tropical Cyclone 05A is in the eastern Arabian Sea, west of India, near 16n/70e, moving slowly to the north. Top winds are 60 mph but may reach 70 mph during the next 24 hours. This system is mainly a threat to shipping, and is not expected to turn toward the coast of India at thia time.

A disturbance is still causing squalls in through the Andaman Islands of the southeast Bay of Bengal. It is somewhat of a risk to shipping in the area. The threat to shipping may increase if the storm develops further, which it may.
